'''Gerrit Bol''' (May 29, 1906 – February 21, 1989) was a Dutch mathematician who specialized in [[geometry]]. He is known for introducing [[Bol loop]]s in 1937,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PPN=GDZPPN00227924X|title=Gewebe und Gruppen|journal=Mathematische Annalen|volume=114|year=1937|pages=414–431}}</ref> and [[Bol's conjecture]] on [[sextactic point]]s.<ref>{{cite news|title=On a conjecture of G. Bol |journal=Math SCAND |volume=40 |year=1977 |pages=194–196 |url=http://www.mscand.dk/article.php?id=2357 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103060824/http://www.mscand.dk/article.php?id=2357 |archivedate=2013-11-03 }}</ref>

==Life==
Bol earned his PhD in 1928 at [[Leiden University]] under [[Willem van der Woude]]. In the 1930s, he worked at the [[University of Hamburg]] on the geometry of [[Web (differential geometry)|webs]] under [[Wilhelm Blaschke]] and later [[projective differential geometry]]. In 1931 he earned a [[habilitation]].

In 1933 Bol signed the ''[[Vow of allegiance of the Professors of the German Universities and High-Schools to Adolf Hitler and the National Socialistic State|Loyalty Oath of German Professors to Adolf Hitler and the National Socialist State]]''.

In 1942–1945 during [[World War II]], Bol fought on the Dutch side, and was taken prisoner. On the authority of Blaschke, he was released. After the war, Bol became professor at the Albert-Ludwigs-[[University of Freiburg]], until retirement there in 1971.
